chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Ubeyda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman who married a man while she had a husband. He said: If her first husband was residing with her in the city where she is, and she can reach him and he can reach her, then upon her is the ruling of the married adulterer, which is stoning.

And if her first husband was absent from her, or was residing with her in the city but they could not reach each other, then upon her is the ruling of the unmarried adulteress, and there is no Li'an between them, nor separation.

I said: Who will stone them or whip them with the Hadd, and her husband does not bring her to the Imam, nor does he intend that from her? He said: The Hadd remains for Allah in her body until one who establishes it does so, or she meets Allah while He is angry with her.

I said: And if she was ignorant of what she did? He said: Is she not in the Dar al-Hijra (era of emigration)? I said: Yes. He said: So there is no woman among the Muslim women today except that she knows that it is permissible for the Muslim woman to have two husbands.
And if the woman, when she commits fornication, says 'I did not know' or 'I was ignorant' that what I did was forbidden, and the Hadd is not established upon her, then the Huddud would be nullified.
ai.seo_question: What is the Hadd punishment for a woman who marries while her first husband is still alive?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *bqa'* (continuity) of the Hadd penalty, noting that the punishment remains incumbent upon the woman's body until either an authority enforces it or she dies while God is displeased with her. It further clarifies that while the first husband's presence determines the severity (stoning vs. flogging), the presumption of knowledge (*'ilm al-ghalib*) among Muslim women renders ignorance an insufficient excuse to waive the penalty, ensuring the legal boundaries are not nullified.
